high: The always-L/mid strategy guarantees adequate framing for every randomized build and posture. Because one L exposure costs only 2 of the 5-unit budget and immediately permits completion, its extra cost has no consequential tradeoff; players can bypass the central collimation judgment.

Image adequacy self-check is bypassable: pressing “use this image” on every result invokes a consequence-free validator that explicitly identifies cutoff or blur. The player can use delivery as an oracle instead of visually judging the image.
medium: The automated QA mischaracterizes always-L as a meaningful risk/reward strategy. It verifies cost and average exposure but never verifies that the cost can affect success, and the tested strategy succeeds on essentially every case.

C_required is weak in practice: opening the order sheet is enforced, but largest-frame selection plus waiting for the visibly labelled stopped phase clears every case without understanding the framing principles. The breathing rule and patient-specific geometry therefore need not both be applied.

A failed delivery does not increment retakes, consume another resource, or otherwise penalize the premature decision; only voluntarily choosing retake increments the counter. This makes repeated delivery guesses strictly advantageous.

The observation-note phase displays the complete, unclipped body rather than the delivered radiograph, so the player assesses haze using information outside the actual acquired image. This weakens imaging-work authenticity.
low: The breathing cycle always starts at the same phase and uses four fixed one-second intervals, making shutter timing highly memorisable across attempts, although a live timing action still remains.

The completion text says a lung is clean or has haze with more certainty than the intended non-diagnostic technologist role warrants, despite the surrounding text correctly assigning diagnosis to the physician.

recommended_actions: Make oversized framing consequential: reduce the budget, require multiple views/tasks within one shared budget, or reject clinically excessive collimation so L/mid is not a universal completion strategy.
Replace the free delivery oracle with an explicit adequacy decision graded after commitment, or charge rejected delivery as a recorded quality failure/retake.
Count every rejected delivery attempt as a retake and attach the same resource or outcome cost as a mistaken self-check.
Use the clipped acquired image in the observation-note phase so findings must be derived from what the player actually captured.
Extend QA with assertions that no single fixed framing clears every case, premature delivery has a cost, and the component state transitions match the simulated strategies.
